quiz.title: Chapter 16 Quiz: The NextGen Bar Exam
quiz.intro: Ten questions on the five named skills, excerpt triage, and the compressed cycle.

items.q: Which list is the chapter’s five named research skills?
options: Issue spotting, IRAC, Bluebooking, citation, memo writing
Ambiguity spotting, intra-jurisdiction source ranking, dispositive fact identification, research gap identification, research sufficiency and closure
Natural language, Boolean, citator, headnotes, key numbers
items.why: The chapter names these five from the NCBE competencies (Five Core Research Skills).

options: Reading a legal text and identifying terms, phrases, or provisions whose meaning requires interpretive research
items.why: Look for undefined terms, vague standards, terms of art, structural ambiguities, and scope questions (Skill 1).

items.q: The chapter’s name for reading every provided source before attempting an answer is:
items.why: Build a mental map of what each source provides, which binds, which persuades, and where the gaps are (Practice Strategies).

items.q: In the convenience-store triage example, the state premises-liability statute that says nothing about third-party crime is:
options: A finding: read for scope, it does not reach the issue, and that is recorded, not discarded
items.why: Naming what a provided source does not reach is part of the triage (Example: Excerpt triage, run once).

items.q: On “which source governs” questions, the chapter says the whole game is:
items.why: Misranking a persuasive decision or an off-point statute as controlling is a leading pitfall (Common Pitfalls).

items.q: Research sufficiency means the materials answer the question when:
options: All questions are answered or identified as open, authorities are validated, the framework is consistent, and counterarguments are addressed
items.why: The sufficiency call must be committed; “probably enough” is not a call (Skill 5; Exercise 16.1).

options: “The law is genuinely unclear” from “I have not yet found the answer”
items.why: This is the line Chapters 8 and 9 drilled (Skill 4).

items.q: A clear statutory provision versus case law interpreting a different statute:
items.why: Mandatory authority from the highest source controls; persuasive authority supports (Identifying the strongest authority).

items.q: The examinee mistake the chapter lists first is:
options: Starting to write before reading every provided source
items.why: That is how examinees miss the one authority that controls the answer (Common Pitfalls).

items.q: The chapter’s claim about bar preparation is that:
options: A separate research prep course is required
Consistent practice of the method’s five steps throughout law school is itself bar exam preparation
Only Part II matters for the exam
items.why: Every move in the compressed cycle is one you have already run at full size (Chapter Recap).

drills.title: Name the Skill
drills.blurb: Eight exam moments. Which of the five named skills is each one exercising?

drills.title: Excerpt Triage
drills.blurb: The compressed cycle on provided materials, in six steps. Put them in order.
